description: This file defines classes and functions for serializing and deserializing non-standard JSON types using a tagging system, including support for types like dict, tuple, bytes, Markup, UUID, and datetime. It is part of the Flask framework's JSON handling utilities.

classes.name: JSONTag
classes.description: Base class for defining type tags for the tagged JSON serializer.

classes.name: TagDict
classes.description: Tag for 1-item dicts with keys matching registered tags, using suffix '__' for serialization.

classes.name: PassDict
classes.description: Tag for general dictionaries, serializing all key-value pairs with tags.

classes.name: TagTuple
classes.description: Tag for tuple objects, serialized as list of tagged items.

classes.name: PassList
classes.description: Tag for list objects, serializing each item with tags.

classes.name: TagBytes
classes.description: Tag for bytes objects, encoded with base64.

classes.name: TagMarkup
classes.description: Tag for Markup objects, serializing via __html__ method.

classes.name: TagUUID
classes.description: Tag for UUID objects, serialized as hex string.

classes.name: TagDateTime
classes.description: Tag for datetime objects, serialized as HTTP date string.

classes.name: TaggedJSONSerializer
classes.description: Serializer class that uses tags to represent non-JSON standard types, supporting registration and recursive untagging.

methods.name: register
methods.description: Register a new tag class with the serializer, optionally forcing overwrite and specifying insertion index.

methods.name: tag
methods.description: Convert a value to a tagged representation if applicable.

methods.name: untag
methods.description: Convert a tagged JSON object back to its original Python type.

methods.name: _untag_scan
methods.description: Recursively untag nested structures in data.

methods.name: dumps
methods.description: Serialize a Python object to a JSON string with tags.

methods.name: loads
methods.description: Deserialize a JSON string, converting tagged objects back to Python types.
